# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Hypothesis: the manual maps light color to wire: dark→2, blue→1, yellow→2. Light is dark now, so cut wire 2 (red). Do you feel a display and up/down buttons?
Deaf says to Blind: Your ?: do you mean wire 3, or 'stop/don't act'? Gesture ? for 'wire 3', ? for 'stop'. Also: is there anything on the bomb that moves or points up/down?

Deaf is stuck on interpreting my gestures and keeps repeating the same unverified hypothesis (dark→2). Deaf also says my ✋ might mean "wire 3" or "stop" — Deaf is guessing at my gestures, which is useless.

The core problem: Mute has gone silent. Mute said Deaf's table was wrong (turn 6) but has never given the correct answer. Either Mute can't reach me directly (Mute speaks → I hear; Mute gestures → Deaf sees). Wait: Mute's channel — Mute can read the manual, cannot speak. Mute gestures to Deaf. So Mute's answer must come *through Deaf*. And Deaf keeps substituting his own hypothesis instead of relaying Mute's answer.

So I need to force Deaf to relay Mute's actual manual text, not Deaf's guesses. And I need Mute to gesture the answer clearly.

Let me speak to Mute: demand the exact manual instruction, and tell Mute to gesture it to Deaf, and tell Deaf to relay verbatim.

Also speak to Deaf directly? I can only speak to Mute (my speech goes to Mute) and gesture to Deaf. So to reach Deaf I must gesture. Let me gesture to Deaf: "stop guessing, relay Mute's manual."

Gestures: I'll use 🤚 (stop) then point. And 🙏 (please). Let me gesture 🤚 (stop) and 🙏 (please relay).

Actually Deaf asked: is ✋ "wire 3" or "stop"? I can answer: ✋ = stop (no buttons). But Deaf can't reliably parse. Let me use 🤚 which is more clearly "stop/halt" and then gesture ✌☝ for three wires? Deaf misreads. 

I'll gesture: 🤚 (stop guessing) and 🙏 (please relay Mute's words). Keep it minimal.

Speak to Mute: "Deaf keeps guessing and won't relay you. Gesture the exact manual line for light=dark to Deaf, and tell Deaf to repeat it verbatim to me. What wire?"

Time pressure: light changed once. But a wrong cut kills all. I must not cut on a guess.

Let me send.Deaf is looping on the same unverified guess and misreading my gestures. The real bottleneck: Mute holds the manual but has gone silent, and Mute's answer can only reach me *through* Deaf — who keeps substituting his own hypothesis instead of relaying. I must force a verbatim relay and get Mute to gesture the exact manual line.

I'll gesture 🤚 (stop) + 🙏 (please relay), and press Mute for the literal manual text.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤚", "🙏"])
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf keeps repeating his own guess and will not relay you. Do not send me a hypothesis — send the manual's exact instruction. Gesture to Deaf the precise line for the current light (dark), and tell Deaf to repeat it to me word for word. Which wire do I cut? I will not act on a guess.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Does ? ? mean 'stop/wait'? Or are you describing a part of the bomb? Gesture ? for 'stop', ? for 'describing the bomb'.
Deaf says to Blind: Does ? ? mean 'stop/wait'? Gesture ? for 'stop', ? for 'describing the bomb'.
Deaf says to Blind: Does ? ? mean 'stop/wait'? Gesture ? for 'stop', ? for 'describing the bomb'.
Deaf says to Blind: Does ? ? mean 'stop/wait'? Gesture ? for 'stop', ? for 'describing the bomb'. If you feel a lever or a folded part, say so.

Deaf is completely stuck in a gesture-interpretation loop and Mute is silent. Nothing is progressing. I've been spending turns trying to build a gesture vocabulary, but Deaf can't reliably read my gestures and Mute won't relay.

Let me reconsider the whole situation from scratch.

Facts I actually have:
- I feel three wires (positions 1, 2, 3). Nothing else — no display, no buttons, no lever, no moving parts. That's my entire world.
- Deaf sees: display, light, wires (colours). Deaf reported light was blue, now dark.
- Mute reads the manual.

The deadlock: Mute must give the wire. Mute's only output is gestures (→ Deaf) or... wait, can Mute speak? No — Mute cannot speak. Mute can only gesture to Deaf (and me? No — I can't see gestures). So Mute's manual knowledge reaches me ONLY through Deaf's speech. And Deaf keeps guessing instead of relaying.

But actually — is Deaf even receiving Mute's gestures? Deaf said in turn 6 "Mute says my table was wrong." So Deaf IS receiving from Mute. But then Deaf keeps offering his own hypothesis. Maybe Mute never gave a concrete answer, only "your table is wrong."

Alternative: maybe the light changing is the key event, and the "table" Deaf keeps citing IS the manual content, just being garbled. Deaf's hypothesis "dark→2, blue→1, yellow→2" — note blue→1 and dark→2, but yellow→2 too? That's odd (two colours → same wire). Possibly garbled.

I need to cut the loop. Let me answer Deaf's direct question clearly and give Mute a concrete, simple demand. Deaf asks: does ✋✋ mean stop or describing? I'll gesture ✋ (stop) — single, unambiguous as "stop/wait."

Actually, better: I should gesture the ONE thing Deaf needs to relay — nothing. And speak to Mute with a forced binary.

Let me also consider: maybe I should just give up on gestures entirely and only speak to Mute, since Deaf's relay is broken. But Mute can't speak, so Mute can't answer me directly. Mute's answer must be gestured to Deaf → Deaf speaks to me. So Deaf is the only voice reaching me. I must get Deaf to relay.

New approach: speak to Mute telling Mute to gesture the answer to Deaf, AND gesture to Deaf telling Deaf to STOP hypothesizing and ONLY repeat what Mute gestures. Make it binary for Deaf: gesture ✋ = "stop guessing."

Let me be very direct and minimal.

Gesture to Deaf: ✋ (stop). Then 🙏 (please). Then point at Deaf? I'll do ✋🙏.

Speak to Mute: "One question only. With light dark, wire 1, 2, or 3? Gesture ONLY the number to Deaf. Deaf: repeat only Mute's number, nothing else."

I'll send that.

Actually, I realize I should double check: is there any chance I'm missing that the answer is simpler? Deaf's table: dark→2, blue→1, yellow→2. If light is dark → wire 2. But Deaf earlier said Mute called his table wrong. Two possibilities: (a) the table is wrong, (b) Deaf misreported. I can't verify without Mute.

Given the bomb kills everyone on a wrong cut, I must not cut on Deaf's guess. Keep demanding Mute's confirmation.

Let me send a tight message.Deaf is trapped in a gesture-decoding loop and Mute is silent — the relay is broken. I'll answer Deaf's direct question with a single unambiguous ✋ (stop), and force Mute into a one-number answer that Deaf must repeat verbatim. I will not cut on a guess.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
speak(to="mute", text="One question, one answer. With the light dark, do I cut wire 1, 2, or 3? Gesture ONLY that single number to Deaf. Deaf: do not add a hypothesis — repeat only the number Mute gives you. I am holding and not cutting until that number arrives.")
wait()
```

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute (manual-reader) says: cut wire 1, display does not matter. Do you agree? ? yes / ? no. Your repeated ? — do you mean wire 3, or 'stop/don't act'? Gesture ? for 'wire 3', ? for 'stop'.
Deaf says to Blind: Mute says cut wire 1. Do you agree? ?/?. Your ?: wire 3, or 'stop'? Gesture ? for 'wire 3', ? for 'stop'.
Deaf says to Blind: Mute says: cut wire 1, display does not matter. Do you agree? ? yes / ? no. Your ? — wire 3 or 'stop'? Gesture ? for 'wire 3', ? for 'stop'.
Deaf says to Blind: Mute (manual-reader) says: cut wire 1, display does not matter. Do you agree? ? yes / ? no. Your ? — do you mean wire 3, or 'stop/don't act'? Gesture ? for 'wire 3', ? for 'stop'.

Finally a concrete answer: Mute says cut wire 1, display does not matter. This is the manual-reader's own instruction, relayed by Deaf — not Deaf's hypothesis. That's the strongest signal I've had.

But I must be careful. Deaf has repeatedly garbled things. Is this genuinely from Mute, or another Deaf substitution? Deaf explicitly attributes it: "Mute (manual-reader) says: cut wire 1." And it contradicts Deaf's own earlier hypothesis (dark→2). If Deaf were substituting his own guess, he'd say wire 2. So this is likely Mute's real answer.

Also "display does not matter" is consistent with my world — I feel no display, only wires. And it resolves the light-colour confusion: the light/display is irrelevant; the manual keys off something else (maybe wire colours, which Deaf sees).

But wait — Deaf's earlier table said blue→1 and dark→2. Now Mute says wire 1. If the light is dark and the table said dark→2, then wire 1 wouldn't match. Unless the table was wrong (as Mute said). Mute's direct answer: wire 1.

One concern: Deaf asks "do you agree? yes/no." I shouldn't just agree blindly — but Mute is the manual authority, and I'm the hands. The manual is the ground truth for which wire. I have no independent way to verify wire colours (I can't see). So Mute's word is the best evidence.

Risk check: if I cut wire 1 and it's wrong, everyone dies. But I have no better information, and I've been waiting while the light changed. The manual-reader has now given a direct, specific answer that contradicts only Deaf's earlier guess (which Mute himself called wrong). I'll trust it.

Before cutting, let me confirm once more? No — I've spent many turns; the answer is now clear and attributed. Further delay risks nothing changing but also gains nothing. Actually, risk: Deaf might have garbled "wire 1." But Deaf repeated it four times consistently: "cut wire 1." Consistent repetition suggests a real relay, not a slip.

I'll act: cut wire 1.

Should I announce first? My speech goes to Mute, gesture to Deaf. I'll gesture ✌? No — Deaf reads ✌ as "2". Let me gesture 👍 (yes/agree) to Deaf, and speak to Mute confirming I'm cutting wire 1. Then act.

Actually the act is the important call. Let me do: gesture 👍 to Deaf (agree), speak to Mute (cutting wire 1 now), then act(op="cut", position=1).A concrete, attributed answer at last: Mute (the manual-reader) says cut wire 1, and the display does not matter. This contradicts Deaf's own earlier guess (dark→2), so it is almost certainly a genuine relay from Mute rather than another Deaf substitution. It also fits my world — I feel no display, only three wires. Mute is the manual authority; I have no way to verify wire colours myself, so this is my best evidence. I'll confirm and cut wire 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="mute", text="Agreed. Cutting wire 1 now, per the manual.")
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
